title: Affine pushforward detects degree-zero concentration
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Then $E$ is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf in degree zero if and only if $Rf_*E$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf in degree zero; in that case the degree-zero sheaf is $f_*E$.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence; Tag 08I8, lemma-affine-morphism (Rf_* reflects isomorphisms on D_QCoh for f affine); Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XC, coherent-lemma-relative-affine-vanishing (R^if_*F = 0 for i>0, F quasi-coherent, f affine)

proof.text: Suppose first that $E$ is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ in degree zero. The affine higher-direct-image statement [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] gives $R^if_*\mathcal F=0$ for $i>0$ and identifies $f_*\mathcal F$ as quasi-coherent. By the definition of $Rf_*$ and its cohomology sheaves, $Rf_*E$ is therefore represented by $f_*\mathcal F$ in degree zero.

Conversely, assume that $Rf_*E$ is represented by a quasi-coherent sheaf in degree zero. The affine derived pushforward t-exactness and conservativity statement [lem-sc-affine-derived-pushforward-t-exact] says that $E$ has the same standard cohomological truncation bounds as $Rf_*E$; hence $E$ has no cohomology outside degree zero and is represented by its degree-zero quasi-coherent cohomology sheaf.

In either direction, the degree-zero cohomology sheaf of $Rf_*E$ is the degree-zero direct image of the representing sheaf, namely $f_*E$; this is the $i=0$ part of the affine direct-image statement [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] together with the definition of the cohomology sheaves of $Rf_*$. Thus the degree-zero sheaf asserted in the statement is $f_*E$.
